26. Edge Weight Normalization
Report me periodic normalization function hai.
Goal:
Global weight values ko drift hone se bachana aur relative ordering preserve karna. fileciteturn34file0L13-L17

Concept:
Current Mean Weight = 1.5
Target Mean Weight = 1.0
scale = 1.0 / 1.5

Then every hierarchical edge:
new_weight = old_weight × scale

subject to:
WEIGHT_MIN
WEIGHT_MAX

[L35] ### 3.2 Data Flow
[L36]
[L37]
[L38] Raw Document (PDF/DOCX/HTML)
[L39]
↓ Layer 1: Validate, detect format, extract text, OCR if needed
[L40] Normalized Text + Metadata
[L41]
↓ Layer 2: Detect layout, segment into blocks, classify types, reading order
[L42] [Page → Region → Block] hierarchy
[L43]
↓ Layer 3: Split sentences, extract concepts/definitions/relations
[L44] KnowledgeUnit objects (candidate concepts)
[L45]
↓ Layer 3: Alias resolution (merge synonyms via MinHash LSH)
[L46] KnowledgeNode objects (canonical, deduplicated)
[L47]
↓ Layer 4: Validate relations against ontology, score confidence
[L48] KnowledgeEdge objects (typed, scored)
[L49]
↓ Layer 5: CPG++ → PRE → HV → FI → CLD (hierarchy construction)
[L50] Knowledge Forest (rooted trees + cross-links)
[L51]
↓ Layer 6: Query → embed → find seeds → traverse → Tree Knapsack selection
[L52] Selected context nodes (within token budget)
[L53]
↓ Layer 7: Build prompt, invoke LLM
[L54]
↓ Layer 7: Verify claims against evidence, bind citations
[L55] Answer with citations + confidence score
[L56]
↓ Layer 8: Log, collect feedback, update forest weights
[L57]

[L207] # SHIA-RAG: Semantic Hierarchy Induction Architecture for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
[L208]
[L209] > Project Type: Minor Project (M.Tech)
[L210] > Date: August 2026
[L211] > Author: [Your Name]
[L212]
[L213] --[L214]
[L215] ## Abstract
[L216]
[L217] Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as the dominant paradigm for grounding Large
Language Model (LLM) outputs in external knowledge. However, current RAG systems universally rely on flat text
chunking — splitting documents into fixed-size segments and retrieving the top-k most similar chunks. This approach
destroys semantic continuity, produces fragmented context, and fails at multi-hop reasoning.
[L218]
[L219] We present SHIA-RAG (Semantic Hierarchy Induction Architecture for Retrieval-Augmented Generation), a
novel 8-layer RAG system that replaces flat chunks with a dynamically constructed Knowledge Forest — a collection
of rooted trees where each node represents a concept (with definitions, aliases, properties, and evidence) and edges
encode hierarchical (IS_A, PART_OF) and semantic (USES, CAUSES) relationships.
[L220]
[L221] SHIA-RAG introduces five novel contributions: (1) Precedence-Constrained Tree Knapsack for context

blob:https://chatgpt.com/e2b31603-f9df-4055-82cd-e524a077a7c4

636/678

03/09/2026, 14:50

Layer Explanation Plan

selection under token budgets, ensuring hierarchical coherence; (2) Self-Evolving Knowledge Forest with a closedloop feedback mechanism that modifies edge weights based on retrieval success/failure; (3) Multi-Objective Energy

[L247] ## 1. Introduction
[L248]
[L249] ### 1.1 Problem Statement
[L250]
[L251] Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become the standard approach for grounding LLM outputs in
external knowledge. The typical RAG pipeline works as follows:
[L252]
[L253] 1. Split documents into fixed-size text chunks (e.g., 512 tokens)
[L254] 2. Embed each chunk into a vector space
[L255] 3. At query time, retrieve the top-k most similar chunks
[L256] 4. Feed these chunks as context to an LLM for answer generation

[L378] ## 13. Conclusion & Future Work
[L379]
[L380] ### 13.1 Summary
[L381]
[L382] This report presents SHIA-RAG, a novel 8-layer Retrieval-Augmented Generation system that replaces flat text
chunks with a dynamically constructed Knowledge Forest. The system introduces five novel contributions:
[L383]
[L384] 1. Precedence-Constrained Tree Knapsack — to the best of our knowledge, the first formulation of RAG
context selection as a precedence-constrained optimization problem
[L385] 2. Self-Evolving Knowledge Forest — to the best of our knowledge, the first closed-loop feedback
mechanism that modifies RAG knowledge structures based on retrieval success/failure
[L386] 3. Multi-Objective Energy Minimization — a formal optimization framework for automated hierarchy
induction combining semantic similarity, depth, confidence, and type coherence
[L387] 4. Adaptive Depth Traversal — query-complexity-aware retrieval depth adaptation for hierarchical RAG
[L388] 5. SHEF Evaluation Framework — to the best of our knowledge, the first benchmark specifically designed for
hierarchical RAG quality
[L389]
[L390] The complete system specification covers:
[L391] - 9 layers (Layer 0-8) with schemas, algorithms, pseudocode, and inter-layer data contracts
[L392] - 12 defined functions with complete implementations
[L393] - 12 relation types across 4 hierarchical and 8 semantic categories
[L394] - 8 schemas covering all data objects from document blocks to query logs
[L395] - A 6-month implementation roadmap with technology stack, folder structure, and CI/CD pipeline
[L396] - A comprehensive evaluation plan with datasets, baselines, ablation studies, and statistical significance
testing
[L397]

[L439] ## 2. Literature Review
[L440]
[L441] ### 2.1 Related Work
[L442]
[L443] #### 2.1.1 Flat-Chunk RAG Systems
[L444]
[L445] The foundational RAG approach was introduced by Lewis et al. (2020), combining dense passage retrieval with
seq2seq generation. Subsequent systems — REALM (Guu et al., 2020), RETRO (Borgeaud et al., 2022), Atlas (Izacard
et al., 2023), and Self-RAG (Asai et al., 2024) — improved retrieval quality, generation faithfulness, and self-

blob:https://chatgpt.com/e2b31603-f9df-4055-82cd-e524a077a7c4

642/678

03/09/2026, 14:50

Layer Explanation Plan

reflection, but all operate on flat text chunks with no structural awareness.
[L446]
[L447] #### 2.1.2 Structured RAG Systems
[L448]
[L449] Recent work has begun exploring structured retrieval:
[L450]
[L451] | System | Approach | Key Limitation |
[L452] |--------|----------|----------------|
[L453] | RAPTOR (Sarthi et al., 2024) | Recursive abstractive processing — clusters chunks and generates summaries
at multiple levels | Top-down summaries only; no concept-level extraction or entity resolution |
[L454] | GraphRAG (Edge et al., 2024) | Builds a knowledge graph from text, retrieves subgraphs | No hierarchy; flat
graph structure; no self-evolution |
[L455] | TreeRAG (Concept) | Organizes documents into topic trees for retrieval | No formal hierarchy induction
algorithm; manual tree construction |
[L456] | HiChunk (LlamaIndex) | Hierarchical chunking with parent-child relationships between chunks | Chunks are
still text fragments, not semantic concepts |
[L457]
[L458] #### 2.1.3 Knowledge Graph Construction
[L459]
[L460] Ontology learning and taxonomy induction have a rich history in NLP:
[L461] - Hearst patterns (Hearst, 1992) extract hypernym relations from text
[L462] - Taxonomy induction (Velardi et al., 2013; Bansal et al., 2014) builds hierarchies from web corpora
[L463] - Knowledge Graph Embedding (TransE, RotatE) learns vector representations of entities and relations
[L464]
[L465] However, none of these systems integrate hierarchy construction with RAG retrieval and self-evolution.
[L466]

[L510] ## 12. Risk Analysis
[L511]
[L512] | Risk | Impact | Probability | Mitigation |
[L513] |------|--------|-------------|------------|
[L514] | LLM extraction errors propagate to forest | High | High | Confidence thresholds, human-in-loop review for
low-confidence nodes |
[L515] | Forest grows too deep (>10 levels) | Medium | Medium | Hard depth limit (configurable, default=8), depth
regularization in energy function |
[L516] | O(N²) operations at scale | High | Medium | LSH for canonicalization, ANN for CPG++, batch processing |
[L517] | Cross-document entity conflicts | High | High | Evidence-weighted consensus voting, temporal versioning,
conflict logging |
[L518] | LLM hallucination in answers | High | Medium | Claim extraction + evidence verification, confidence scoring |
[L519] | Cold start (new domain, no forest) | Medium | Low | Bootstrap from domain ontology (e.g., Wikipedia
categories) |
[L520] | Database sync issues (3 DBs) | Medium | Medium | Saga pattern for distributed transactions, idempotent
operations |
[L521] | Self-evolution reinforces wrong paths | Medium | Medium | ε-greedy exploration (ε=0.1), periodic weight
normalization, anomaly detection |

[L611] #### Multi-Tree Knapsack Selection
[L612]

[L613] For multi-seed queries, candidates may span multiple trees. The algorithm:
[L614]
[L615] 1. Group candidates by tree root
[L616] 2. Allocate token budget proportionally to each tree
[L617] 3. Run Tree Knapsack on each tree independently
[L618] 4. Merge results and trim to total budget
[L619]
[L620] ```python
[L621] def multi_tree_knapsack(self, candidate_nodes, budget):
[L622] tree_groups = {}
[L623] for node in candidate_nodes:
[L624] root = self.forest.find_root(node)
[L625] tree_groups.setdefault(root.id, []).append(node)
[L626]

[L739] ## 1. Introduction
[L740]
[L741] ### 1.1 Problem Statement
[L742]
[L743] Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become the standard approach for grounding LLM outputs in
external knowledge. The typical RAG pipeline works as follows:

blob:https://chatgpt.com/e2b31603-f9df-4055-82cd-e524a077a7c4

649/678

03/09/2026, 14:50

Layer Explanation Plan

[L744]
[L745] 1. Split documents into fixed-size text chunks (e.g., 512 tokens)
[L746] 2. Embed each chunk into a vector space
[L747] 3. At query time, retrieve the top-k most similar chunks
[L748] 4. Feed these chunks as context to an LLM for answer generation
[L749]
[L750] While effective for simple factoid questions, this flat-chunk approach suffers from five fundamental
limitations:
[L751]
[L752] | Problem | Description | Impact |
[L753] |---------|-------------|--------|
[L754] | Broken semantic continuity | Fixed-size splits cut across paragraphs, definitions, and logical units | LLM
receives incomplete or incoherent context |
[L755] | Duplicate/fragmented information | The same concept may appear in multiple chunks with slight variations
| Token budget wasted on redundancy |
[L756] | Fixed granularity | All chunks are the same size regardless of content complexity | Cannot retrieve at
different levels of abstraction |
[L757] | Weak multi-hop reasoning | No explicit connections between chunks | Cannot follow reasoning chains (e.g.,
A → B → C) |
[L758] | No cross-document fusion | Chunks from different documents are independent | Cannot merge knowledge
from multiple sources |
[L759]
[L760] ### 1.2 Proposed Solution: SHIA-RAG
[L761]
[L762] SHIA-RAG (Semantic Hierarchy Induction Architecture for Retrieval-Augmented Generation) addresses all five
limitations by replacing flat text chunks with a structured Knowledge Forest:
[L763]
[L764]
[L765] Traditional RAG:

Document → [Chunk₁, Chunk₂, ..., Chunkₙ] → Top-k → LLM

[L766] SHIA-RAG:
[L767]

Document → Knowledge Forest (concepts + relations) → Adaptive Traversal → LLM

[L768]
[L769] The system:
[L770] 1. Extracts knowledge — concepts, definitions, relations, and evidence from raw documents
[L771] 2. Builds a Knowledge Forest — a hierarchy of semantically linked concept nodes organized as rooted trees
[L772] 3. Retrieves knowledge nodes — by traversing the hierarchy (parents, children, cross-links) with adaptive
depth
[L773] 4. Selects context optimally — using a Tree Knapsack algorithm that respects hierarchical precedence
constraints
[L774] 5. Generates verified answers — with claim-level evidence verification and citation binding
[L775] 6. Learns from feedback — a self-evolution loop that updates edge weights based on retrieval success/failure

[L1034]
[L1035] | Risk | Impact | Probability | Mitigation |

[L1036] |------|--------|-------------|------------|
[L1037] | LLM extraction errors propagate to forest | High | High | Confidence thresholds, human-in-loop review for

[L1038] | Forest grows too deep (>10 levels) | Medium | Medium | Hard depth limit (configurable, default=8), depth

[L1039] | O(N²) operations at scale | High | Medium | LSH for canonicalization, ANN for CPG++, batch processing |

[L1042] | Cold start (new domain, no forest) | Medium | Low | Bootstrap from domain ontology (e.g., Wikipedia
categories) |
[L1043] | Database sync issues (3 DBs) | Medium | Medium | Saga pattern for distributed transactions, idempotent
operations |
[L1044] | Self-evolution reinforces wrong paths | Medium | Medium | ε-greedy exploration (ε=0.1), periodic weight
normalization, anomaly detection |
